A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mini-Monkey and provide readable, corresponding methods, equations, figures and experiments. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, although v3 contains an unresolved 'appendix ??' reference.

before.justification: v1 reports original Mini-Monkey benchmark results, cropping and compression ablations, cross-model experiments, and a qualitative example in Tables 1–6 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and ablation results in Tables 1–8, including additional fine-tuning, model-capacity and crop-count experiments.

M1.justification: MSAC becomes CIP, retaining the detailed, adaptive and global image views and complementary cropping principle. The InternVL2-2B pipeline and SCM using the first two LLM layers remain. Expanded descriptions of grid selection and token weighting do not establish a new architecture, objective or method component.

E1.justification: Evaluation coverage is unchanged: all eight general/math and nine document/OCR benchmarks already appear in v1 Tables 1–3. v3 newly identifies training datasets, including DVQA, GeoQA+ and LLaVA-150K (zh), whereas v1 leaves its training data unspecified. Whether training-domain or language coverage actually changed cannot be determined.

E2.justification: v3 adds QWEN-VL-7B to Table 1, TextSquare-7B to Table 2, and the underlying InternVL2-2B baseline to Table 3's accuracy comparison. The transfer comparison also adds LLaVA-OV-0.5B and InternVL2-1B/8B alongside retained models in Table 6. Together these substantially broaden the direct comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 introduces CIP-by-fine-tuning configurations, additional model-size evaluations, and baseline crop-count settings of 18, 24, 32 and 48. It also revises stated detailed/adaptive crop ranges from 8–24/1–8 in v1 Section 4.1 to greater than 9 through 24/3–8 in v3 Section 2.1. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 5 separates CIP's effects from fine-tuning alone, while Table 8 tests whether merely increasing crop count explains the gains. The transfer ablation expands to additional architectures and model capacities. These substantially extend the mechanism and applicability analyses; the earlier SCM ablation and qualitative case are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional v3 results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Reported Mini-Monkey results change, including OCRBench 802 to 806 in Table 2 and ChartQA accuracy 57.9 to 67.3 in Table 3. New controls and model comparisons add substantial results; the newly included InternVL2-2B scores 67.6 on ChartQA accuracy, above Mini-Monkey. Version-to-version increases are not established as identical-setting gains. SCM results remain unchanged between v1 Table 6 and v3 Table 7.

T1.justification: v3 corrects SCM's attention-map dimensions from T × L to (L2 + L3 + T) × L1, replaces the undefined Vt with Vd, and specifies averaging across queries to obtain per-token selection weights. These are limited mathematical specification corrections and additions; no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claim that complementary scales alleviate crop-induced semantic damage remains. v3 adds explicit claims about training-free CIP and its beneficial interaction with fine-tuning, while revising headline performance claims. The change from 13 to 17 counted benchmarks does not represent newly evaluated datasets.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking overlapping-crop redundancy to hallucinations and adaptive crops to simulated cross-window feature interaction. It interprets the new controls as evidence that CIP aids fine-tuning and provides benefits beyond crop count. The conclusion adds a limitation discussion concerning parameter-free image construction and future trainable feature pyramids.

D1.justification: Where v1 primarily specifies the backbone and crop settings, v3 first identifies six training datasets, AdamW and a base learning rate of 4e-8. It also supplies more explicit aspect-ratio selection and SCM aggregation instructions. These address important implementation omissions, although training duration and mixture proportions remain unspecified, and the accuracy-details reference now points to an absent appendix. The code link and eight-RTX-3090 claim are retained.

R1.justification: The dedicated document-understanding survey in v1 Section 2.2 is removed, including its discussions of LayoutLMv3, UDOP, Donut and Pix2Struct. v3 refocuses positioning on high-resolution cropping, adds works such as SPHINX, Qwen2-VL, Oryx and LLaVA-OneVision, and expands the contrast with fixed multi-scale processing.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. MSAC/layers become CIP/groups, an explicit contribution list is added, and the document-understanding subsection and standalone Discussion section disappear. This is a broad reorganization of existing narrative, beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The page template and three illustrations are retained, with localized relabeling and diagram revisions in Figures 1–2 and relocation of Figure 3. v3 adds Tables 5 and 8, expands comparator and transfer tables, and relocates the unchanged SCM table from Table 6 to Table 7. The overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: The fine-tuning controls in Table 5 and matched-crop-count comparison in Table 8 address important alternative explanations that v1 left untested. Adding the underlying InternVL2-2B baseline to Table 3 and broadening transfer tests substantially strengthen the empirical case, supported by better implementation disclosure. These gains outweigh the unresolved appendix reference and residual reporting errors, such as Table 5 labeling 800 versus 784 as '+17'; higher scores alone do not establish the improvement.
